title: Internal hom of module objects
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a closed symmetric monoidal Grothendieck abelian category whose tensor
product is additive in each variable. Write $\underline{\Hom}(X,-)$ for the right adjoint
of $X\otimes-$ and $\mathrm{ev}\colon X\otimes\underline{\Hom}(X,Y)\to Y$ for the counit.
Let $\mathcal R$ be a commutative monoid object. For $\mathcal R$-module objects $M$ and
$N$, let $\Hom_{\mathcal R}(M,N)$ be the equalizer of the two maps
$$
\underline{\Hom}(M,N)\rightrightarrows\underline{\Hom}(\mathcal R\otimes M,N)
$$
adjoint to the two composites
$$
\mathcal R\otimes M\otimes\underline{\Hom}(M,N)\xrightarrow{\mathcal R\otimes\mathrm{ev}}
\mathcal R\otimes N\xrightarrow{\gamma_N}N,
\qquad
\mathcal R\otimes M\otimes\underline{\Hom}(M,N)\xrightarrow{\gamma_M\otimes1}
M\otimes\underline{\Hom}(M,N)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{ev}}N .
$$
Let $\mathcal R$ act on $\Hom_{\mathcal R}(M,N)$ through its action on $N$. Then
$\Hom_{\mathcal R}(M,-)$ is right adjoint to $M\otimes_{\mathcal R}-$, so the symmetric
monoidal category $(\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C),\otimes_{\mathcal R})$ of
[def-sfb-modobj-symmetric-tensor] is closed. Here $\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)$ is
abelian by [lem-sfb-modobj-abelian].

proof.text: The category $\mathcal C$ has small colimits by [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. For each $X$, $X\otimes-$ has the right adjoint specified in the statement. The natural symmetry gives $-\otimes X\dashv\underline{\Hom}(X,-)$ as well: precompose $L\otimes X\to Y$ with $\beta_{X,L}$ and then use the given adjunction. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] to these adjunctions. Both tensor functors preserve small colimits, in particular coequalizers and finite colimits. Thus [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor] and [def-sfb-modobj-symmetric-tensor] apply, and [lem-sfb-modobj-abelian] gives the abelian category of modules. All indexing categories used here are small; the coequalizer diagram is the finite parallel-pair category.

source.place: definition and imported proof, expanded by Q09

proof.text:
Put $H=\underline{\Hom}(M,N)$ and $K=\underline{\Hom}(\mathcal R\otimes M,N)$, and call the two displayed arrows $p,q:H\rightrightarrows K$, with $p$ obtained from the action on $N$ and $q$ from the action on $M$. Equalizers exist: by [def-sp-abelian] take $E=\ker(p-q)$, with inclusion $i:E\to H$. In what follows all associators and unitors are inserted in the displayed order of the factors, and interchanging factors means the specified symmetry. Write $\epsilon=\mathrm{ev}\circ(1_M\otimes i):M\otimes E\to N$. Naturality and injectivity of the adjunction bijection identify $pi=qi$ with
$$\epsilon\circ(\gamma_M\otimes1_E)=\gamma_N\circ(1_{\mathcal R}\otimes\epsilon)\quad\text{on }\mathcal R\otimes M\otimes E.\tag{B}$$
Here the right adjoint, its natural hom-set bijections, and their inverse $h\mapsto\mathrm{ev}\circ(1\otimes h)$ are the closed structure assumed in the statement, not an additional existence assertion.

source.place: definition and imported proof, expanded by Q09

proof.text:
Define $a_H:\mathcal R\otimes H\to H$ to be the transpose of
$$M\otimes\mathcal R\otimes H\xrightarrow{\beta_{M,\mathcal R}\otimes1}\mathcal R\otimes M\otimes H\xrightarrow{1\otimes\mathrm{ev}}\mathcal R\otimes N\xrightarrow{\gamma_N}N.$$
It satisfies the module axioms of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Indeed, uncurrying $a_H\circ(\eta\otimes1_H)$ gives $\gamma_N\circ(\eta\otimes\mathrm{ev})=\mathrm{ev}$ by the unit law of $N$. Uncurrying the two associativity composites from $\mathcal R\otimes\mathcal R\otimes H$ gives, after moving $M$ past the two scalar factors, respectively $\gamma_N\circ(\mu\otimes\mathrm{ev})$ and $\gamma_N\circ(1\otimes\gamma_N)\circ(1\otimes1\otimes\mathrm{ev})$. They agree by associativity of $N$. Equality of the transposes proves the asserted laws.

source.place: definition and imported proof, expanded by Q09

proof.text:
The morphism $t=a_H\circ(1_{\mathcal R}\otimes i):\mathcal R\otimes E\to H$ equalizes $p,q$. Here is the complete check after uncurrying, on $\mathcal R\otimes\mathcal R\otimes M\otimes E$. Use slot notation: $r,s,m,e$ label tensor factors, $s m$ means $\gamma_M(s,m)$, and $r\epsilon(m,e)$ means $\gamma_N(r,\epsilon(m,e))$; these are composites of morphisms, not elements of objects or a test for equality on points. The two uncurried composites are equal by
$$r\epsilon(s m,e)=r(s\epsilon(m,e))=(rs)\epsilon(m,e)=(sr)\epsilon(m,e)=s(r\epsilon(m,e)).$$
The first equality is (B), the second and last are the associativity axiom for $N$ from [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and the middle equality is $\mu\circ\beta_{\mathcal R,\mathcal R}=\mu$, the assumed commutativity of $\mathcal R$. Thus the equalizer property gives a unique $a_E:\mathcal R\otimes E\to E$ with $ia_E=t$. This constructs precisely the action through $N$ in the statement.

source.place: definition and imported proof, expanded by Q09

proof.text: The action $a_E$ is unital and associative: postcompose its unit equation and its associativity equation with $i$, replace $ia_E$ by $a_H(1\otimes i)$, use the corresponding equations for $a_H$ from step 3, and cancel the monomorphism $i$. For a module morphism $f:N\to N'$, postcomposition induces $H\to H'$ and carries $E$ to $E'$: the equality $f\gamma_N=\gamma_{N'}(1\otimes f)$ takes (B) to (B) for $N'$. It is linear for the target actions because both sides, after uncurrying, are $f\gamma_N(1\otimes\mathrm{ev})=\gamma_{N'}(1\otimes f\mathrm{ev})$. Cancellation of $i'$ makes the induced $E\to E'$ linear. Identities and composites follow by postcomposing with $i'$ and uniqueness of equalizer lifts. Hence $E=\Hom_{\mathcal R}(M,N)$ is a module and is functorial in $N$. These checks use exactly the module and module-morphism equations of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects].

source.place: definition and imported proof, expanded by Q09

proof.text:
Fix a module $L$. Let $Q=L\otimes_{\mathcal R}M$ with projection $\pi:L\otimes M\to Q$ as in [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor]. By its coequalizer property, a map $u:Q\to N$ of $\mathcal C$ is equivalent to $g=u\pi:L\otimes M\to N$ satisfying
$$g(rl,m)=g(l,rm).\tag{bal}$$
Here and below the same slot convention as in step 4 specifies equalities of tensor composites; the action on the right of $L$ in the defining parallel pair is $\gamma_L\beta_{L,\mathcal R}$. The projection and the action through $L$ satisfy $\gamma_Q(1\otimes\pi)=\pi(\gamma_L\otimes1_M)$, with the canonical reordering of factors. Thus linearity of $u$ implies
$$g(rl,m)=r g(l,m).\tag{lin-L}$$
Conversely (lin-L) implies linearity of the descended $u$: precompose its proposed linearity equation with $1_{\mathcal R}\otimes\pi$. This is an epimorphism because it is a coequalizer, by step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]; a coequalizer is epi by uniqueness of its factorizations. Hence the two composites agreeing implies the linearity equation. Equations (bal) and (lin-L) together are equivalent to (lin-L) and
$$g(l,rm)=r g(l,m).\tag{lin-M}$$
This last equivalence just replaces one side of (bal) using (lin-L).

source.place: definition and imported proof, expanded by Q09

proof.text:
Transpose $g\beta_{M,L}:M\otimes L\to N$ to $h:L\to H$. The equalizer property says that $h=iv$ for a unique $v:L\to E$ exactly when $ph=qh$. Uncurrying the latter equality gives
$$\gamma_N\circ(1_{\mathcal R}\otimes g)\circ(1_{\mathcal R}\otimes\beta_{M,L})
=g\circ\beta_{M,L}\circ(\gamma_M\otimes1_L)$$
as maps $\mathcal R\otimes M\otimes L\to N$. This is exactly (lin-M) after reordering the tensor factors. No condition about linearity in $L$ was used in this step; it expresses only that $h$ takes values in the equalizer.

source.place: definition and imported proof, expanded by Q09

proof.text:
The transpose $h:L\to H$ is linear for $a_H$ exactly when $h\gamma_L=a_H(1_{\mathcal R}\otimes h)$. Uncurrying gives the equation on $M\otimes\mathcal R\otimes L$ whose two sides, in slot notation, are $g(rl,m)$ and $r g(l,m)$; the definition of $a_H$ in step 3 gives the second composite. This is precisely (lin-L). If $h=iv$, then
$$i\,v\gamma_L=h\gamma_L,\qquad i\,a_E(1\otimes v)=a_H(1\otimes h).$$
Since $i$ is mono, $v$ is linear exactly when $h$ is linear. Thus the module-morphism definition of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and the two transpose calculations give: $g$ satisfies (lin-L) and (lin-M) if and only if its transpose uniquely lifts to a module morphism $v:L\to E$.

source.place: definition and imported proof, expanded by Q09

proof.text:
Steps 6--8 give a bijection
$$\Hom_{\mathcal R}(L\otimes_{\mathcal R}M,N)\cong\Hom_{\mathcal R}(L,E).$$
Explicitly the forward map takes $u$ to the equalizer lift of $\operatorname{curry}(u\pi\beta_{M,L})$. The reverse map takes $v$ to the coequalizer descent of $\mathrm{ev}(1_M\otimes iv)\beta_{L,M}$. Currying and uncurrying are inverse, and $\beta_{M,L}\beta_{L,M}=1$, so the two constructions are inverse after precomposing with $\pi$, respectively postcomposing with $i$. The universal properties cancel $\pi$ and $i$. For a module morphism $b:L'\to L$, the transpose formula takes $g(b\otimes1_M)$ to $hb$. For a module morphism $f:N\to N'$, it takes $fg$ to $\underline{\Hom}(M,f)h$. These are the naturality identities of the given ambient adjunction; uniqueness of both lifts therefore gives naturality in $L,N$.

source.place: definition and imported proof, expanded by Q09

proof.text:
Finally [def-sfb-modobj-symmetric-tensor] supplies the natural module isomorphism $\beta^{\mathcal R}_{L,M}:L\otimes_{\mathcal R}M\to M\otimes_{\mathcal R}L$. Precomposition with it identifies
$$\Hom_{\mathcal R}(M\otimes_{\mathcal R}L,N)\cong\Hom_{\mathcal R}(L\otimes_{\mathcal R}M,N).$$
Compose with step 9. Its inverse uses $\beta^{\mathcal R}_{M,L}$, and naturality follows from naturality of that symmetry and of step 9. This is the adjunction $M\otimes_{\mathcal R}-\dashv\Hom_{\mathcal R}(M,-)$ with the specified equalizer right adjoint. A monoidal category is closed precisely when each $M\otimes-$ has such a right adjoint; hence the given symmetric monoidal structure is closed.
